thread:
incident-bot: Pager: Elevated GPU OOM rate on stream-dispatch-eu-west-1 cluster. 3m window: 38% decode request drops, 27 nodes with oom events. Potential customer impact: cust-foo, cust-bar. Runbook: /runbooks/gpu-oom-streaming. Paging oncall.

oncall-anna: I'm oncall. linking logs and starting triage. @eng-sre-josh can you grab pod-level OOMs and recent deploys?

eng-sre-josh: looking now. Seen a lot of CUBLAS allocation failures and kernel retries. grabbing crashlog from pod decode-pod-7:
```
2026-03-17T12:03:21Z ERROR decode: CUDA error: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED
stack: at runtime::alloc_tensor(..)
kmod: gpu0 free=120Mi total=40Gi
```

ml-runtime-kim: quick note — router telemetry shows a spike in requests with max_tokens set to very large values from a single API key in the last 7m. Could be runaway generation header bypass.

support-lee: Support ticket flood: multiple customers seeing 500s and truncated streams. CS is asking for ETA to share with customers.

oncall-anna: mitigation plan:
- throttle ingress for that API key (apply per-key qps cap)
- enable token-cap enforcement at edge (fallback to 4096)
- route new requests to fallback model-smaller until we stabilize
- drain and restart most-affected nodes

eng-sre-josh: executing now: `kubectl cordon node/gpu-node-23 && kubectl drain node/gpu-node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then restart pods with `kubectl rollout restart deploy/decode-service` on eu-west-1. Also applying iptables rate limit at ingress.

incident-bot: Action taken: key throttled, token-cap enforcement toggled (edge override -> 4096), 6 nodes cordoned and restarted. Telemetry still shows OOMs but dropping.

ml-runtime-kim: root-cause hypothesis: a recent canary for a customer-specific routing policy accidentally forwarded an unvalidated max_tokens header (client-provided) directly to the decoder, bypassing router caps. That allowed extreme generation lengths and caused KV cache growth -> OOM cascades.

eng-sre-josh: confirmed: policy revision r2041 introduced header passthrough for X-Client-Max-Tokens. Reverting that patch now.

oncall-anna: reverting patch r2041 and reapplying validated-path. Rolling back canary on eu-west-1.

cust-ops-sam: Cust Ops notified top-affected customers with a short explainer and ETA: "mitigations applied, rolling restarts ongoing, ETA ~15-25m". Customers asked for root cause once stabilized.

support-lee: posting interim CS blurb to internal status: "We experienced GPU OOMs causing dropped streaming responses due to unusually large max_tokens values from a routing misconfig. We're throttling and routing to smaller models while rolling back the change. We'll follow up with RCA."

eng-sre-josh: new telemetry 10m post-mitigation: request drops down to 3%, OOMs limited to <2 nodes. Logs show no new CUBLAS alloc failures on restarted nodes.

oncall-anna: good. Next actions:
- full rollback confirmed, monitor 60m
- add ingress validation for X-Client-Max-Tokens (reject > 1e5)
- postmortem and corrective runbook update (assignments: kim + josh)
- outreach: cust-ops to send formal customer note in 2 hours

ml-runtime-kim: will own the validation PR and add unit tests for header passthrough. linking an eval to ensure fallback model quality okay.

cust-ops-sam: I'll prepare the customer follow-up and CS summary.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Page closed at 1719510600. Please update runbook and postmortem when available.

oncall-anna: Thanks team. I'll hand this off to followup rotation. :white_check_mark:"
